module_title: Genetics & Evolution: Mendelian Principles, DNA Basics & Origin of Life
introduction: This foundational level explores the biological rules of inheritance laid down by Gregor Mendel, the fundamental structural blueprint of DNA (the molecule of life), and the biochemical origin of life on Earth. Mastery of basic genetic terminology and evolutionary evidences is essential.

core_concepts.title: Mendelian Genetics: Principles of Inheritance
core_concepts.description:
Gregor Mendel (Father of Genetics) conducted hybridization experiments on garden peas (Pisum sativum) for 7 years (1856-1863). He selected 7 pairs of contrasting traits (Stem height, Flower color/position, Pod shape/color, Seed shape/color).
1. Law of Dominance: Characters are controlled by discrete units called factors (genes). In a dissimilar pair of factors (heterozygous), one dominates (dominant) the other (recessive).
2. Law of Segregation: Alleles do not blend. During gamete formation, the factors or alleles of a pair segregate (separate) from each other such that a gamete receives only one of the two factors. This law is universal and has NO exceptions.
3. Law of Independent Assortment: When two pairs of traits are combined in a hybrid, segregation of one pair of characters is independent of the other pair of characters.

core_concepts.title: Molecular Basis: Structure of DNA
core_concepts.description:
DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is a long polymer of deoxyribonucleotides. 
Watson-Crick Model (1953): DNA is a double helix. Two polynucleotide chains run anti-parallel ($5' \rightarrow 3'$ and $3' \rightarrow 5'$). The backbone is made of sugar-phosphate, and the bases project inside. 
Base Pairing: Adenine pairs with Thymine via TWO hydrogen bonds ($A=T$), and Guanine pairs with Cytosine via THREE hydrogen bonds ($G\equiv C$). 
Chargaff's Rule: In a double-stranded DNA, the ratio of Adenine to Thymine, and Guanine to Cytosine is constant and equals one ($A+G = T+C$). 
Dimensions: Pitch of the helix is $3.4 \text{ nm}$ ($34 \text{ \AA}$). The distance between a base pair is $0.34 \text{ nm}$. There are roughly 10 base pairs per turn.

core_concepts.title: Origin of Life
core_concepts.description:
Oparin-Haldane Theory: The first form of life could have come from pre-existing non-living organic molecules (e.g., RNA, protein) via chemical evolution. The primitive Earth had reducing conditions: high temperature, volcanic storms, reducing atmosphere containing $CH_4, NH_3, H_2$, and water vapor (No free $O_2$).
Miller-Urey Experiment (1953): Simulated primitive Earth conditions. Created electric discharge in a closed flask containing $CH_4, H_2, NH_3$ (in ratio 2:1:2) and water vapor at $800^\circ\text{C}$. They observed the formation of Amino Acids, proving chemical evolution.

core_concepts.title: Evidences for Evolution
core_concepts.description:
1. Paleontology: Study of fossils. Shows that life forms varied over time and certain forms are restricted to specific geological time spans.
2. Homologous Organs: Same basic structural plan and origin, but perform different functions. Example: Forelimbs of whales (swimming), bats (flying), cheetahs (running), humans (grasping). Indicates Divergent Evolution.
3. Analogous Organs: Different anatomical structure and origin, but perform the same function. Example: Wings of butterfly and wings of birds. Indicates Convergent Evolution.

important_entities.name: The Nucleosome
important_entities.key_fact: The basic repeating structural unit of chromatin.
important_entities.significance: In eukaryotes, DNA is highly negatively charged. It is wrapped around a positively charged histone octamer (composed of two molecules each of H2A, H2B, H3, and H4). A typical nucleosome contains $200 \text{ bp}$ of DNA helix. Histones are rich in basic amino acid residues: Lysine and Arginine.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often use 'gene' and 'allele' interchangeably. A **Gene** is the fundamental unit of inheritance that codes for a particular trait (e.g., Gene for plant height). An **Allele** is an alternative version of that exact same gene (e.g., Allele for Tallness 'T' vs. Allele for Dwarfness 't'). Alleles are located at the exact same locus on homologous chromosomes.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
To remember which type of evolution creates which organ:
- **H**omologous organs $\rightarrow$ **D**ivergent evolution (**HD**)
- **A**nalogous organs $\rightarrow$ **C**onvergent evolution (**AC**)

exam_strategy_tips: In monohybrid crosses, always remember the ratios. The phenotypic ratio is 3:1 (Tall:Dwarf). The genotypic ratio is 1:2:1 (TT:Tt:tt). For a dihybrid cross, the phenotypic ratio is 9:3:3:1. To quickly find the number of types of gametes produced by a genotype, use the formula $2^n$, where $n$ is the number of heterozygous loci (e.g., AaBbCc has 3 heterozygous loci $\rightarrow 2^3 = 8$ types of gametes).
